summary: A sandbox adds real friction and can still fail through kernel escapes, allowed channels, poisoned inputs or unsafe exported artifacts.

points.text: Containers share the host kernel, and every virtualization or syscall-emulation layer has vulnerabilities; calling the environment a sandbox can create a false security boundary.
Useful coding tasks often need package registries, source hosts, test services and credentials, so broad egress exceptions can recreate the exfiltration path the sandbox was meant to close.
Measured gVisor overhead and VM startup or image costs can make strong isolation too expensive for short, high-volume tasks.
A clean runtime does not protect against malicious dependencies, prompt injection in repository files or harmful patches that pass through an approved export channel.
